response_text:
Benefits:
- You have greater timing precision - threads can be given timeslices as small as 0.1ms instead of 1ms, giving you finer granularity on CPU allocation.
- You have a more responsive system - high-priority tasks get CPU time mostly quicker because the maximum amount of time before the system takes that CPU time away drops from 1ms to 0.1ms
- You have better real-time performance - since time-sensitive operations have tighter timing guarantees.
Downsides:
- You create more CPU overhead - when SysTick interrupts occur 10x more frequently, that is 10x more CPU cycles spent handling interrupts.
- You create more power consumption - the processor wakes up more often to service timer interrupts
- You create significant context switching overhead - When threads require more than the period (0.1ms) to do something useful, they have to spend more time switching context than doing any work
- You introduced timer resolution that exceeds hardware capabilities - not all ARM processors can issue reliable 0.1ms interrupts.
